analysis.title: The CUDA Moat Drained In 3 Days: JPM's Cembalest Says Jensen Is Nvidia's Smaller Problem
key_insights: Cembalest tallied frontier-lab compute agreements with deployment from 2026 onward: about 44GW in total, of which Nvidia GPUs are 12.1GW (28%), Broadcom custom chips 23%, AMD 18%, Amazon Trainium 16%, Google TPUs 14%, Cerebras 2%. Silicon Analysts put Nvidia's share of AI chip revenue at 80-90% in 2024-2025.

Of the seven biggest buyers of accelerators (five hyperscalers and two frontier labs), only SpaceX is not trying to build its own chip, so most buyers are designing a way around Nvidia's 75% gross margins.

Epoch AI's new inference index, which scores memory and chip-to-chip communication along with raw throughput, puts AMD's MI455X at roughly 2.9x a GB300 and Nvidia's Vera Rubin VR200 at roughly 2.2x (values read off the chart). Cembalest says Rubin Ultra 'may change that when rolled out in 2027.'

A frontier lab told Cembalest that onboarding models onto AMD GPUs, which took 6-12 months a year ago, now takes 3 days using the lab's latest AI model for the engineering work. Cembalest says AMD's MI455X results may have eroded at least part of Nvidia's tokens-per-watt and CUDA software advantage.
On SemiAnalysis's inference model, a Google TPU7x beats Nvidia's GB300 NVL72 on tokens per dollar at every speed except the slowest. The benchmark model is Qwen 3.5 397B, a Chinese open-weight model.

Cembalest calls the Chinese open-weight community 'one of Nvidia's core markets.' It 'consumes the majority of tokens' on OpenRouter, and its models track the closed frontier on Epoch's capabilities index.

Per an Institute for Progress report, 36% of China's projected end-2027 AI compute is already inside China (made there, imported legally or smuggled), and Nvidia is 'a major supplier, willingly or not' to the latter two. SemiAnalysis estimates 1.5GW of restricted Nvidia chips have ended up in China.

Remote access to US AI chips is 32% of China's projected compute, and three-quarters of China's overseas compute sits in Southeast Asia. Cembalest points to the Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which passed the House 369-22 without a Senate vote, as the tool aimed at that slice.

The article reports that Commerce issued an interim final rule on the morning of Nov 17 closing the 'cloud loophole.' It requires a license to ship advanced chips to any data center supplying more than 12 million TPP to China-headquartered firms (roughly 750 H100s) and imposes a blanket license requirement on Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil unless the buyer is US-headquartered. Existing operators have 90 days. This is ZeroHedge's addition, not part of Cembalest's note.

Cembalest says Nvidia under Huang was 'sharply at odds with political forces in the US that favor ring-fencing China.' The share of Nvidia revenue billed to Singapore addresses rose from 8% to 22% after the Biden controls, and in July 2025 Nvidia stopped breaking out the figure.

Cembalest expects that if remote-access curbs work, Chinese companies will have more incentive to develop their own accelerators. Z.AI, DeepSeek and Meituan all cited training and inference on Huawei Ascend NPUs in 2026.

Cembalest does not call a collapse. Nvidia earned 83% of AI chip revenue from 2023 to 2025 at 75% gross margins, chip design cycles are long, and he finds the stock 'interesting for long term holders' at 32% below its all-time high with a PEG of 0.2x, the cheapest large AI stock by a wide margin.
ZeroHedge argues a 0.2x PEG assumes consensus growth holds while both demand legs (frontier labs and Chinese open-weight buyers) are weakening. This is the article author's view, not Cembalest's.

The article says the spy allegation against Huang is weaker than Cembalest's note assumed: the Washington Post reported Rubio reworked a CIA memo that did not reach that conclusion, DOJ has not confirmed it, and Trump said 'I don't know that she was a spy at all.' Commerce published its rule anyway.
Colette Kress holds her first earnings call as interim CEO the day after publication. The article suggests listening for any mention of Southeast Asia revenue.

market_movers.rationale: Cembalest finds the stock 'interesting for long term holders' at 32% below its all-time high with a PEG of 0.2x. He also calls the shifting competitive landscape 'in some ways just as notable a risk for investors as its management change.' No formal rating or target is stated.
Epoch AI's inference index puts the MI455X at roughly 2.9x a GB300, and a frontier lab can now onboard models onto AMD GPUs in 3 days. AMD holds 18% of frontier-lab compute agreements.
SemiAnalysis's model has the TPU7x beating the GB300 NVL72 on tokens per dollar at all but the slowest speeds. TPUs are 14% of frontier-lab compute agreements.
Broadcom custom chips are 23% of frontier-lab compute agreements, the largest share after Nvidia's 28%.
Amazon's Trainium is 16% of frontier-lab compute agreements.
Goldman's Jim Schneider warned Nvidia's 'operations in certain jurisdictions could face more scrutiny going forward.' The Commerce rule puts Southeast Asian data-center demand under license.

sector_views.rationale: Cembalest sees Nvidia's share eroding as frontier labs diversify to AMD, Broadcom, Amazon and Google silicon, but does not call a collapse given Nvidia's 83% revenue share in 2023-2025 and long chip design cycles.

earnings_insights: Nvidia earned 83% of AI chip revenue from 2023 to 2025 at 75% gross margins (Cembalest). Silicon Analysts put the 2024-2025 share at 80-90%.

Colette Kress holds her first earnings call as interim CEO the day after the Nov 17, 2026 publication date, per the article. The article suggests listening for any mention of Southeast Asia revenue, since Nvidia stopped breaking out the figure in July 2025.
Nvidia trades at a PEG of 0.2x, 32% below its all-time high, per Cembalest. The valuation is a trailing market figure, not an earnings estimate.
risk_factors: Frontier labs shifting compute to AMD, Google, Amazon, Broadcom custom silicon and their own chips, cutting Nvidia's share of announced 2026+ deployments to 28%.
Loss of the CUDA software switching cost as AI-assisted engineering shortens model onboarding on AMD GPUs to about 3 days.
US export licensing on remote access to chips, which may cut Nvidia demand from China-linked buyers in Southeast Asia and Brazil.
Chinese buyers moving to Huawei Ascend and other domestic accelerators.
Loss of political capital after Huang's exit, with Nvidia having lost its lobbying fight against the rule.
Nvidia no longer discloses revenue billed to Singapore (stopped July 2025), which limits visibility into exposure.
Possible federal restrictions on open-weight models, which the article argues would reduce demand from Chinese open-weight users.
The 0.2x PEG depends on consensus growth numbers that the article argues are at risk.
charts_described: Pie chart of frontier-lab compute agreements from 2026: Nvidia 28% (12.1GW of roughly 44GW), Broadcom 23%, AMD 18%, Amazon Trainium 16%, Google TPUs 14%, Cerebras 2%.
Epoch AI inference index: AMD MI455X at roughly 2.9x a GB300, Nvidia Vera Rubin VR200 at roughly 2.2x (read off the chart).
Pie chart of China's projected end-2027 AI compute: 36% inside China, 32% remote access to US AI chips, and three-quarters of overseas compute in Southeast Asia.
geopolitical: Commerce interim final rule closing the 'cloud loophole': a license is required to ship advanced chips to data centers supplying more than 12 million TPP to China-headquartered firms, with a blanket license requirement for Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil unless the buyer is US-headquartered. Existing operators have 90 days.
Remote Access Security Act (RASA) passed the House 369-22 and has not had a Senate vote. Cembalest says China hawks 'appear to have the upper hand right now in DC.'

Huang's resignation, and the allegation that he or Nvidia was tied to a spy, which the article says is now contested (Washington Post report on Rubio and a CIA memo, no DOJ confirmation, Trump's comments).
Chinese open-weight AI models, and the article's claim that a federal crackdown on open weights may follow Huang's exit.
Smuggling and routing of restricted Nvidia chips to China through Singapore, including the Megaspeed allegations from Culper Research (Alibaba-funded and controlled customer).
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Jim Schneider warned on Friday that Nvidia's 'operations in certain jurisdictions could face more scrutiny going forward.'

tension_points.bull_case: Cembalest finds the stock 'interesting for long term holders' at 32% below its all-time high and a 0.2x PEG, with 83% AI chip revenue share in 2023-2025, 75% gross margins and long chip design cycles.
tension_points.bear_case: Frontier labs are at only 28% Nvidia in announced compute agreements, AMD's MI455X leads Epoch's inference index, and new US licensing curbs hit Chinese open-weight demand. The article argues the 0.2x PEG assumes consensus growth that both demand legs undermine.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rubin Ultra rollout in 2027, which Cembalest says 'may change' the inference performance picture. The article also points to the interim CEO's earnings call the day after publication, specifically any disclosure on Southeast Asia revenue.
